v1.0.68 — Splash readiness fix: the splash now reads a real HTTP status from `/api/status` and navigates only on a true `200`, instead of guessing from an unreadable opaque response.

### Fixes

- **"Still starting — poll #N" hang fixed at the source (splash navigation gate).** v1.0.67 papered over the symptom with a self-refreshing "Starting…" page, but the underlying defect was in `App.tsx`: it polled `/api/status` with `fetch(..., {mode:"no-cors"})`, whose response is **opaque** — JavaScript cannot read the status code or even reliably tell a settled fetch from a rejected one. So the splash could neither distinguish a `503` ("alive but still running `init_db()`/migrations") from a `200` ("ready"), nor dependably trigger its navigation, leaving the user stuck on the spinner. The splash now issues a **real CORS fetch** (no `no-cors`) and navigates to the dashboard **only when `response.ok` is true** (HTTP `200`, which Flask returns only once `_server_ready` flips). While the sidecar is still extracting (connection refused) or mid-init (`503`), it simply keeps polling. To let the cross-origin webview (`tauri://localhost`) read the response, the public health endpoints (`/api/status`, `/api/status/full`, `/api/modes` — no PII, already token-exempt) now send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on both their `503` and `200` responses; `flask-cors` was never configured for plain HTTP routes. The v1.0.67 hold-until-ready page remains as defense-in-depth.
